Cosmic Selection Realism: A Response to Sharon Street

Sharon Street’s Darwinian Dilemma argues that moral realism faces a serious problem from evolutionary theory. Either evolution shaped our moral beliefs independently of objective moral truth—making their reliability an implausible coincidence—or evolution tracked moral truth, which seems scientifically mysterious. In either case, realism appears unstable.

Cosmic Selection Realism rejects the dilemma by redefining the relationship between moral truth and evolutionary success. The key move is simple: moral truth is not independent of survival. Rather, moral systems are objectively better insofar as they enable the long-term survival and flourishing of a civilization across existential threats. Evolution does not accidentally track moral truth; it is one layer of a broader selection process that filters out moral systems incapable of sustaining a species.

(1/3)

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

replies.text:
Imagine a universe—or even multiple cosmic cycles—in which civilizations rise and fall. Species that adopt short-sighted, self-destructive value systems eliminate themselves. Species whose moral structures foster cooperation, coordination, technological advancement, and resilience survive and expand. Over vast timescales, only those value systems compatible with sustained survival remain instantiated. Moral truth is thus not a mysterious, stance-independent property floating free of natural processes; it is the set of evaluative principles that withstand cosmic selection pressure.

On this view, there is no coincidence. Evolution shapes our moral psychology because survival requires certain forms of social organization and cooperation. If our moral system proves inadequate and humanity is extinguished by competitors—alien or otherwise—then that failure would demonstrate its inferiority. Survival is not merely evidence of moral adequacy; it is constitutive of it.

(2/3)

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

replies.text:
This position denies that morality must stand in judgment over survival. Rather, survival is the precondition of all moral practice. A species that ceases to exist cannot instantiate value. Therefore, the preservation and expansion of value-bearing agents is normatively primary. Moral norms are objectively ranked by their capacity to secure that preservation across long horizons.

Street’s dilemma depends on separating evolutionary success from moral truth. Cosmic Selection Realism dissolves that separation. Moral systems are not validated by tracking independent truths; they are validated by surviving the ultimate test: continued existence in a competitive universe.

In this way, realism is preserved without mystery. Moral truth is neither coincidental nor metaphysically obscure. It is what endures.

(3/3)
